title: Combat stats and power
summary: How rolled stats, equipment, quality, class multipliers, and damage traits combine.

sections.title: Eight stats
paragraphs: Health is damage capacity, Armor reduces ordinary incoming damage, Strength/Dexterity/Magic/Wisdom supply class power and skill checks, Energy limits adventurer activity, and Combat Power is a separate bonus added to a human’s main combat stat.
An unclassed human uses the highest of Strength, Dexterity, and Magic; ties favor Strength, then Dexterity. A class with an assigned PowerStat uses that instead, including Wisdom for cleric classes.

Human power = round((main stat + Combat Power bonus) × class multiplier × exhaustion multiplier). At zero energy, a human with an energy pool uses an exhaustion multiplier of 0.75. A nonhuman combatant instead uses round(Combat Power stat × its type multiplier). Base damage = round(power × active damage-trait multiplier). Activities then apply their own damage scaling and random rolls.

sections.title: Rolls and quality
paragraphs: Initial combatant stats range from floor(0.75 × declared base) through ceil(1.333 × base), using rounded interpolation. Energy has a fixed declared base. The basic Adventurer has base 100 Health, 100 Energy, and 40 Strength, Dexterity, Magic, and Wisdom.

For human stats, add stored base and all equipment contributions, apply active stat traits, then multiply by human quality and round. Energy is rounded without human-quality multiplication. A human with zero stored base Energy remains without an energy pool even if equipment supplies Energy. Health also receives the Human Health prestige multiplier before quality.

Equipment has independent quality and rolls. Its final stats are added before the wearer-quality multiplier, so both can compound. Health and energy are stored as fractions; changing the maximum retains the fraction.

sections.title: Class power multipliers
paragraphs: These declared values precede damage traits.

rows: Guardian, Battlemaster / Thief, Ranger / Elementalist, Warlock

sections.title: Critical damage
paragraphs: Critical Hit rolls a 5% × active trait quality chance whenever its damage multiplier is evaluated. A success doubles the current damage multiplier. Multiple sources of this same trait keep only the highest-quality active source. The weapon critical enchantment supplies this trait.

title: Armor and damage reduction
summary: The exact armor curve, unarmored penalty, and damage-processing order.

sections.title: Armor curve
paragraphs: For Armor A ≤ 200, ordinary incoming damage is multiplied by 0.5^(A/200). Above 200, first replace A with 200 + (A − 200)^0.8, then apply that exponential. This gives diminishing returns beyond 200.

Exactly zero Armor adds an extra ×2 penalty. Armor-ignoring attacks skip both the curve and zero-armor penalty. Active damage-taken traits apply afterward; the result is rounded and subtracted from health. An incoming value of exactly zero returns immediately.

sections.title: Roles and category
paragraphs: Tank multiplies damage taken by 0.75. Guardian with a Shield divides it by 1 + 0.1 × trait quality. These apply after armor and also protect against armor-ignoring attacks.
Armor category is distinct from the numerical Armor stat. Light, Medium, and Heavy tags affect advancement and certain traits. The numerical stat controls the damage curve.

title: Skill tests and elemental resistances
summary: Check probability, group checks, and the scope of resistance.

sections.title: Checks
paragraphs: Base success chance = clamp(stat ÷ difficulty, 5%, 95%). Skill-test traits modify this afterward. The four skill-critical traits each add 0.4 × trait quality for their matching stat; the final chance is not re-clamped to 95%. The random helper guarantees success when a final probability reaches 1.

Dungeon individual difficulty is integer StageDifficulty ÷ 4; group difficulty is integer StageDifficulty ÷ 3. Most group challenges let members try in order until one succeeds. Clear Rubble instead uses individual difficulty even though any member can save the group.

sections.title: Resistance
paragraphs: Fire, Shadow, and Poison resistance each use reduction = 0.3 + 0.2 × active trait quality, giving 50% at quality 1. The matching hazard multiplies its damage by 1 − reduction. Identical resistance traits keep the highest-quality source, not their sum.

Resistance is requested explicitly by particular hazards rather than universally applied to every elemental-sounding attack. Tank Shadow Damage computes Shadow resistance for its display but does not multiply the actual damage by it in this implementation. The formula contains no explicit upper clamp.

title: Traits and party buffs
summary: Where trait strength comes from and how repeated effects combine.

sections.title: Sources
paragraphs: Traits come from archetypes, classes, equipment, enhancements, and temporary party buffs. Archetype traits use character quality. Declared class traits are instantiated at quality 1, so training does not directly strengthen their percentage formulas; it still improves underlying stats.

Equipment traits use item quality; enhancement traits use enhancement quality. A group buff retains its source trait quality. Repeated copies of the same trait keep only the highest quality. Different traits modify their shared value in stored order.

sections.title: Party application and clearing
paragraphs: At dungeon start every member applies group effects to every member, including themselves. Quest and War Effort intake apply the current members’ effects to the incoming member. Thus a newly added aura source should not be assumed to buff all earlier quest or war members retroactively.

ActivityCompleted increments Level and refreshes traits while clearing temporary buffs. Full Healers are healed completely. The Level counter itself is not an automatic per-level stat formula here; quality training is separate.
Equipment changes refresh traits while retaining stored buffs. Removing a buff removes one stored entry; consumed-aura behavior also depends on refresh and cleanup calls.

title: Tanks, healers, and party formation
summary: Tank qualification, targeting odds, and automatic healing.

sections.title: Tank role
paragraphs: Fighter-archetype humans qualify as Tanks with an offhand Shield and Heavy armor qualification. This includes Fighter-derived classes. Tank reduces damage taken by 25%. The first qualifying member is the dungeon’s designated tank.

Ordinary dungeon hits select that tank with 85% probability on bosses or 65% on other stages, otherwise they select a random member. The random selection can also choose the tank. Scripted tank hazards use their own direct selection.
The displayed distance rank puts Tanks first, then melee or unarmed humans, then ranged humans. Ordinary targeting uses the probabilities above rather than a general front-row shield rule.

sections.title: Standard healing
paragraphs: Base healing starts at Wisdom. If the caster has Healer and combat power exceeds Wisdom, add half the difference using integer division. Apply healing-done multipliers and round. The normal spell heals base healing ÷ 10 using integer division, with the recipient’s healing-taken traits applied afterward.

It chooses the eligible member with the lowest health fraction; full-health and Exhausted members are excluded. A dungeon uses its first Healer, and can stay on a cleared stage while that caster continues finding wounded targets. The final stage ends before this healing phase.

Quest progress ticks have a 25% chance to request that spell. Wars allow a rounded one-Healer-per-five-soldiers limit, clamped to 1–10, randomly excluding excess healers each tick. Inquisitor has Minor Healer rather than the full role.

title: Adventurer classes and advancement routes
summary: The complete class tree and its equipment conditions.

sections.title: First specialization
paragraphs: With Training Grounds specialization research, an Adventurer is checked halfway through training unless the energy payment just exhausted it. The first matching declared advancement wins.

rows: Main weapon’s declared main stat Strength; Heavy armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Dexterity; Medium armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Magic; Light armor qualification
Main weapon’s declared main stat Wisdom; no armor condition

sections.title: Quest branches
paragraphs: Fighter branches to Guardian or Battlemaster; Rogue to Thief or Ranger; Mage to Elementalist or Warlock; Cleric to Ritualist or Priest. The eight advancement quests change only members whose type exactly matches the required base class. Repeat quest rewards retain the advancement effect.

sections.title: Final specializations
paragraphs: Arena advancement checks choose the first eligible declared route after a bout.

rows: Arena; equipped main-hand item has positive actual Strength appraiser stat

sections.title: Armor qualification
paragraphs: Only Head, Chest, and Off Hand participate. At least one of Head or Chest must be present, and at least one must match the requested category. None of the checked pieces may have a category above the requested one. A lighter partner piece is allowed; a completely unarmored character does not qualify.
A weapon’s main stat is the first largest declared BaseStats entry in stat enum order. Inquisitor’s condition is different: it checks the actual equipped weapon’s Strength value.

title: Class trait effects
summary: Implemented role bonuses for every specialization, separate from power multipliers.

sections.title: Parent traits
paragraphs: Here q is trait quality, normally fixed at 1 for declared class traits. Final classes retain their parent trait.

sections.title: Final effects
paragraphs: These add to retained parent traits.

rows: 50% chance per dungeon healing hook: heal lowest-health eligible ally other than self for base healing ÷ 20
Armor gains actual offhand Shield Armor × q
Without Heavy armor qualification: damage multiplier × (1 + 0.2q)
Dungeon group buff: boss damage multiplier × (1 + 0.03q)
Dungeon Tank group buff: boss damage taken × (1 − 0.1q)
Dungeon damage multiplier gains +0.15q; companion is not a separate combatant
Combat Power bonus gains 0.5 × current Strength × q; Minor Healer role
33.3% chance per dungeon healing hook: heal every member for base healing ÷ 40
Dungeon Tank group buff: healing received on boss stages × (1 + 0.1q)

sections.title: Healer inheritance
paragraphs: Cleric, Ritualist, Priest, Shaman, Evangelist, and Lightbringer declare full Healer. Inquisitor instead has Minor Healer: 50% chance on dungeon-healing and war hooks to heal an eligible ally other than self for base healing ÷ 25. Fighter-archetype descendants can gain Tank through equipment regardless of branch.

title: Equipment slots, hands, and armor affinity
summary: Slot unlocks, weapon conflicts, equipment rolls, and enhancements.

sections.title: Unlocks
paragraphs: Head, Chest, Main Hand, and Off Hand are available by default. Food requires Campfire, Adventure Supplies, or Kitchen; Potion requires Adventure Supplies or Alchemist; Amulet/Ring require Jeweler; Trinket requires Inventor; Scroll requires Scribe.

The equipment gate supports a per-type EquipmentAllowed predicate, but the extracted source contains no assignments to it. Class affinity is primarily an advancement or trait condition rather than a general ban on other equipment.

sections.title: Weapon handling
paragraphs: Greatsword, Bow, Rifle, Staff, and Battleaxe are two-handed. Sword and Dagger are ambidextrous. Shield, Tome, and Focus are Off Hand. Bow, Rifle, Staff, and Wand are ranged for distance rank.
HasWeapon requires a main-hand WeaponItemType. HasDualWield counts more than one such weapon entry. HasShield searches for any Shield weapon. Adding equipment removes conflicts and refreshes traits.

sections.title: Equipment and enhancements
paragraphs: Equipment stat ranges are floor(base × 0.9 × item quality) to ceil(base × 1.1 × item quality). Integer rolls exclude the upper endpoint when bounds differ. Updating equipment quality rerolls these base stats. Enhancement stats are added afterward.

Without multi-enhancement research only one enhancement is allowed. With it, one enhancement per EnhancementType is allowed; duplicate types remain disallowed. Equipment and enhancement traits also contribute their own effects.

Each flat enhancement stat is round(declared enhancement stat × enhancement quality) before being added to the equipment. This differs from the equipment’s own rolled base stats. Quality-adding enhancements affect the item through their crafting workflow; trait quality remains the enhancement source’s quality.

title: Training Grounds and quality growth
summary: Sessions, dummies, food, repeat energy costs, and specialization timing.

sections.title: Session
paragraphs: A session has 10 training ticks, normally every 2 ÷ Speed seconds. A manual action independently has a 50% chance to tick each occupied slot. The Capacity property starts at 3 and rises to 5 with research; intake scans the full five-slot array, so the property alone does not establish an enforced cap.
Each tick requests quality gain of QualityPerTick × building quality, affected by training traits, then awards a random half-to-full share. QualityPerTick is 0.02 without a dummy, 0.04 with one.

Ordinary humans get full gain in their first session, half in their second, and zero from the third onward. Adventurers retain full gain. A nonhuman dummy takes trainee base damage ÷ 10 on ticks with positive gain multiplier; dead dummies are removed.

sections.title: Energy and food
paragraphs: Each tick costs 2 × (1 + TrainingCount) Energy before traits. With food research and Food equipped this is halved; automatic training also performs a second tick for food-bearing trainees each cycle. Food is consumed at completion while that technology is active.

At halfway, specialization research checks advancement if the energy payment did not exhaust the trainee. Exhausted trainees are removed. Finished trainees wait for output space, receive ActivityCompleted, and increase TrainingCount (ordinary humans stop incrementing at 3).

sections.title: War cleanup
paragraphs: War Effort separately cleans non-adventurer humans with TrainingCount above 4: the count becomes 4 and quality is capped at 1.5. This differs from ordinary training diminishing returns.

title: Arena combat and training
summary: Damage, bout-ending conditions, training ticks, and survivor outputs.

sections.title: Attacks
paragraphs: Arena accepts two combatants and its normal update is blocked until Eastern war stage 4 is held. Each fighter applies group buffs only to itself. Attacks occur every 2 ÷ Speed seconds.

Each base damage is integer-divided by 10, then rolled from that value ÷ 1.2 to ×1.2 before armor and damage-taken traits. Both attack values are calculated before damage is applied. Trait hooks run after both hits.

sections.title: Ending a fight
paragraphs: Normal bouts end when a human is below 10% health or a nonhuman dies. Humans that reached zero in normal mode receive a small 2–4 health heal at the next stopping check. Blood Sport waits for a death; if both die, one randomly receives the small heal.

The 10-tick counter limits training and energy deductions, not total bout duration. After it reaches zero, attacks continue until a health ending condition. Opponents whose damage rounds to zero or whose healing outpaces damage may stall.

Eligible humans gain a random half-to-full share of the quality request for each of those first 10 attacks. They pay 3 × (1 + ArenaCount) Energy. Adventurers stay eligible across bouts; ordinary humans train only on their first. Other combatants pay the base energy cost when they have an energy pool.

rows: 0.06; actual quality gain still requires an eligible human

sections.title: Outputs
paragraphs: Only living, non-Exhausted humans return: adventurers repeatedly, ordinary humans only from their first arena visit. Resolution waits for eligible outputs to have room. Returning humans receive ActivityCompleted and ArenaCount increases.

The winner uses higher health fraction; ties select slot 2. Arena and ArenaWin advancement routes are checked in declaration order after output handling. The bout then pays its audience reward and clears both slots.

title: Arena audience income
summary: How initial health, weapons, fighter types, and upgrades determine bout payment.

sections.title: Reward multiplier
paragraphs: At fight start, multiply both fighters’ current health fractions. Halve that result for each human without a main-hand weapon. This initial value is retained until resolution, so starting wounded reduces the entire bout’s reward.

At resolution, multiply by 1 + 0.1 × Arena Cashier upgrade count. Each Adventurer then contributes ×1.2; each other human contributes ×1.1; nonhumans add no type multiplier. With Blood Sport, a multiplier above 1 receives another ×1.25.

sections.title: Payment currency
paragraphs: Currency is selected with successive independent 25% checks, gated by strict reward thresholds. First try Ducats if the multiplier exceeds 1.5; if that fails or is unavailable, try Rings above 1.25, then Crowns above 1.09. Otherwise pay Gold.

Payment count is round(10,000 × final reward multiplier ÷ selected currency’s gold value). This changes the denomination, while the formula targets the same gold-equivalent amount. A resolved bout sets a four-second cooldown.

title: Quest Board progress and repeat costs
summary: Five-adventurer work groups, progress-based hazards, energy, training, and blocked outputs.

sections.title: Progress
paragraphs: A Quest Board holds up to five adventurers and updates once per second. Each living, non-Exhausted participant contributes base damage ÷ its individually adjusted quest difficulty. For quests with DurationMultiplier exactly 1, the contribution is capped at 2 per participant per update.

A contribution below 1 is penalized: the adventurer takes a random damage roll around 0.5 ÷ its original contribution (range ÷1.5 to ×1.5), then contributes only half the original amount. This makes badly underpowered adventurers both slower and vulnerable.

Progress is shared. Challenges and trait hooks execute once for each whole progress boundary crossed, not once per real second. Faster groups therefore run more hazard and energy ticks per second while finishing sooner. Progress may overshoot the target.

sections.title: Energy and completion
paragraphs: Each whole progress tick costs EnergyPerTick × (1 + that adventurer’s QuestCount), before positive-energy-loss trait modifiers. The default EnergyPerTick is 0.2. Hazards may add to it. A 25% chance on each progress tick asks the first Healer to cast.

Completion waits until every output buffer is empty. It subtracts the quest’s current TickDuration from shared progress, grants first or repeat rewards, increments global completion count, then returns all current members through the adventurer output.

Each returned member receives the quest’s completion callback, ActivityCompleted, +1 QuestCount, and a random half-to-full quality gain from TrainingAdded × training upgrade multiplier. Default TrainingAdded is 0.12; each Quest Training upgrade adds +0.5 to the multiplier. Coin upgrades add +0.1 each to the currency multiplier.

sections.title: Repeated duration
paragraphs: TickDuration = round(BaseDuration × DurationMultiplier^global completion count). Only quests with a multiplier other than 1 grow this way, and those quests also bypass the normal contribution cap of 2. This count belongs to the quest metadata, so different boards share its first-clear and repeat history.

Dead or Exhausted participants are removed on progress processing. Completion checks and per-progress hazard loops have a specific ordering; avoid assuming survival and removal happen immediately after each individual hazard.

title: Quest challenges, rewards, and permanent discounts
summary: What specialization markers and quest hazards actually do, including first-clear economics.

sections.title: Quest hazards
paragraphs: Triggered challenges independently roll each whole quest progress tick. Dangerous has the default 5% trigger chance: each participant takes random ordinary damage around (15 + quest difficulty ÷ 50) × (quest difficulty ÷ participant base damage), with a ÷1.3 to ×1.3 range.

Exhausting triggers every progress tick and adds 10% of the normal quest energy cost. Dexterity Energy triggers at the default 5% chance; each participant failing a Dexterity test against raw quest difficulty pays 15 times normal quest energy cost.

Fighter, Rogue, and Mage specialization markers halve effective difficulty for matching archetypes. Cleric specialization quarters it. These alter progress contribution and the low-performance penalty, but Dangerous and Dexterity Energy use the raw quest difficulty. Increase Duration is a descriptive marker; the actual duration formula is the quest’s DurationMultiplier.

sections.title: First and repeat rewards
paragraphs: Currency and item rewards are granted once per completed group, not once per participant. Advancement rewards inspect every group member and change only exact matching class types. First-clear and repeat reward lists can differ.

Currency reward count is rounded after multiplying by the board or dungeon’s CoinLootMultiplier. Item reward count is fixed. Item quality uses the output element’s quality: when above 1, it rolls reward quality × random((1 + element quality) ÷ 2, element quality). The default reward quality is 1.
Each Quest Item Loot and Dungeon Item Loot upgrade contributes +0.1 element quality. It improves the quality of reward items rather than multiplying their declared counts.

sections.title: Permanent economic rewards
paragraphs: Clear Mines first sets the Iron Ore discount flag; the resource cost multiplier becomes 0.25. Each repeat multiplies it by another 0.95: 0.25 × 0.95^repeat counter. Its difficulty is 470, base duration 180, and duration multiplier 1.05.

Forest Evangelism first halves forest-worker cost, with each repeat multiplying by another 0.95: 0.5 × 0.95^repeat counter. It has difficulty 600, base duration 180, duration multiplier 1.05, and the Cleric specialization marker. These discounts multiply other applicable cost calculations.

sections.title: Quest roster
paragraphs: Ordinary quests are Patrol Market, Exterminate Rats, Dispel Library, Clear Mines, Forest Evangelism, and Mercurial Reagents. Eight further quests provide the intermediate class branches. Use each quest’s entity page for exact first/repeat items and research gates.

title: Dungeon runs, stages, loot, and retreat
summary: The five-adventurer expedition loop and what happens between fights.

sections.title: Starting
paragraphs: A dungeon node needs five Adventurer inputs, an available selected dungeon, no active party, and the full supply currency payment. It consumes all five inputs and applies party buffs. Ticks occur every two seconds; this tick interval is fixed in Dungeon.Update rather than divided by the node’s Speed.

Each dungeon has eight stages, alternating nonboss and boss. Stage health = BaseHealth × StageDifficulty. Nightmare endgame adds its own health multiplier. Every active combat tick increments StageTick, then adds random party base damage ÷ 1.2 to ×1.2 to stage progress. Challenges and combat traits execute next.

Ordinary party damage follows: at least one hit occurs, with a 50% continuation chance after each hit. That gives an average two hits but no fixed maximum. Dead/Exhausted members are then removed. Losing the last member records a wipe and resets the run.

sections.title: Damage and boss escalation
paragraphs: Dungeon damage rolls between integer StageDifficulty ÷ 50 and integer StageDifficulty ÷ 33, multiplied by the requested hazard multiplier. On boss stages the multiplier also gains ×(1 + 0.015 × StageTick). This grows every active combat tick, so stalled boss fights become more dangerous.
Normal hits use tank-targeting odds. Individual challenges can bypass armor, target everyone, consume energy, or impose separate skill checks.

sections.title: Loot and between-stage healing
paragraphs: Reaching stage health sets three cooldown ticks before looting. Before granting rewards, all ItemReward outputs for the stage must exist and have no buffered items. A blocked output delays loot and energy payment, then retries.

Successful loot grants every stage reward, deducts the stage EnergyCost from each member (default 10), invokes the stage callback, and increments clear count. After limit-break checks, healing traits and the first full Healer can act. A cleared stage advances when the standard Healer has no eligible wounded target.

The final stage records victory and clears the party before the normal healing phase. Successful expeditions do not output the adventurers. A wipe or victory sets five cooldown ticks and resets stage progress to the beginning.

sections.title: Retreat and extra loot
paragraphs: Retreat refunds each supply currency by the fraction 1 − zero-based CurrentStage ÷ total stages, truncating each refund to an integer. It clears the party and run with two cooldown ticks. Changing dungeon selection mid-run invokes retreat.

Trash Loot upgrades independently give a 5% × upgrade-count chance each nonboss combat tick to award 25% of every Ducat reward on that stage. This explicit 0.25 reward call does not use the node CoinLootMultiplier. Normal stage currency rewards do use the coin multiplier, which grows by 0.1 per coin upgrade.

title: Dungeon challenge reference
summary: Every dungeon hazard’s trigger chance, target, check, and effect.

sections.title: How to read the table
paragraphs: All probabilities are independent per active combat tick when the hazard is listed on the current stage. D means one fresh GetDungeonDamage(1) roll with that stage’s current difficulty and boss escalation. A ×multiplier requests a roll at that multiplier; final armor and traits are applied afterward unless marked armor-ignoring.

Individual difficulty = integer stage difficulty ÷ 4; group difficulty = integer stage difficulty ÷ 3. A group check stops at the first successful member. A random target is selected from current party members.

sections.title: Physical and skill hazards
paragraphs: These use ordinary armor processing.

paragraphs: These ignore armor and its unarmored penalty. Resistance is applied only as specified.

sections.title: Injected poison
paragraphs: The Inject Poison debuff itself deals 0.2D armor-ignoring damage on each dungeon combat hook. Its tick does not ask for another Poison resistance value. The initial injection avoids adding the debuff whenever the target already has any positive poison reduction. Multiple identical debuffs keep the highest trait quality rather than stacking duplicate active traits.

title: Energy, death, and dungeon limit breaks
summary: What exhaustion removes, how recovery works, and when Faith can prolong an expedition.

sections.title: Health and exhaustion
paragraphs: Health and Energy initialize at full fractions. A combatant is Dead when its health fraction is zero. A character with a positive energy pool is Exhausted at zero energy unless its LimitBreak flag is active. Nonhumans normally have no energy pool, and ordinary humans with zero base Energy ignore Energy equipment.

Energy loss is clamped to the 0–100% fraction. Positive loss passes through energy-loss traits; negative loss restores energy without those modifiers. Healing passes through healing-taken traits and clamps to maximum health. No separate persistent injury-status system is present in these core combatant classes; remaining health is the injury measure.

Quest and training systems remove exhausted participants instead of automatically resting them. Arena only returns living, non-Exhausted eligible humans. War removes soldiers on death. Dungeon parties are consumed by defeat, victory, or retreat rather than sent through a survivor output.

sections.title: Limit Break
paragraphs: With Dungeon Limit Break, a member at zero energy can remain active while other party members still have energy. Its human combat power is reduced to 75%. If the whole party reaches zero energy, the run records a wipe and resets even with Limit Break.

With the Faith-based second limit break, an energy-loss call that reaches zero tries to spend round(requested energy loss × 5) Faith. On success it sets the member to exactly 1 CurrentEnergy. This is not a full refill and is not priced only on the missing portion. It can be invoked by stage costs or challenge losses.

A stage completion deducts energy before CheckForLimitBreak; this check can remove zero-energy members or end a fully exhausted run. Consumables that restore energy during later healing hooks cannot be assumed to rescue members already removed by earlier checks.

sections.title: Completion recovery
paragraphs: ActivityCompleted raises Level, clears temporary buffs, and fully heals full Healers; it does not restore Energy. Potions, energy amulets, and energy scrolls supply explicit recovery effects. Other humans retain their remaining health when returned from training, quest, or arena activities.

title: War Effort combat, medals, and defense
summary: How army power becomes territorial progress and why completed fronts still need soldiers.

sections.title: Army progress
paragraphs: War updates every two seconds. Combine carried PartialProgress with each soldier’s base damage. A human without a main-hand weapon contributes half. Adventurers additionally multiply contribution by lerp(0.5, 1, energy fraction). This energy weighting is separate from zero-energy human power loss.

Enemy strength is interpolated between the current stage’s StartStrength and EndStrength using progress fraction. While accumulated power is strictly greater than current strength, subtract that strength and gain one progress point, recalculating as stages change. Retain the rounded remainder for future updates.

If the update gains no progress points, it loses one instead. Partial progress is still retained. A new conquered stage begins at 5 progress. Losing below zero falls back one stage with progress set to its maximum minus 5; the first stage floors at zero.

sections.title: Defense
paragraphs: After every stage is cleared, the front becomes a defense meter. Required strength uses half the last stage’s EndStrength, except the North keeps full EndStrength. The defense meter can fall back into the final stage if lost. Holding territory is therefore an ongoing supply commitment.
The final defense meter’s base maximum is 100. Nightmare scaling can alter endgame maximum progress. Defense combat uses lower damage-hit and medal chances than active conquest.

sections.title: Damage, healing, medals
paragraphs: Each soldier has a 66% chance per conquest update to be hit, or 33% in completed-front defense. The damage basis interpolates from the previous stage’s EnemyDamage to the current one where applicable, then rolls from that value to ×1.6, truncates to an integer, and uses normal armor/traits. Dead soldiers are removed.

A human carrying any WeaponItemType can generate a medal on a 20% conquest chance, or about 6.67% during defense. Its death adds another medal unit when that armed-human condition is met. The total is rounded after multiplying by the front’s MedalsMultiplier.
Full Healers cast once subject to the one-per-five-soldiers rounded limit, clamped 1–10. War trait hooks then run, including potions, passive regeneration, and other special effects.

sections.title: Inputs and remains
paragraphs: War Effort accepts combatants; Adventurers require the adventurer-to-war technology. Intake continues while that front’s CanProgress condition allows it. The passive recruitment technology gives a separate 5% chance at one Medal per new soldier.

With a remains output present and empty, a soldier death has a 50% chance to create Human Remains carrying the soldier’s quality. This branch is not restricted to human item types by its code. Barracks has base output rate 0.5 × Speed and quality resource cost multiplier 2.

sections.title: All four war fronts
paragraphs: These are base values before active Nightmare scaling. Ironcrag Siege intake is gated by currently holding Siege of Yensburg stage 4. Final defense keeps full last-stage strength in Ironcrag and halves it in other fronts.

title: Adventure potions, auras, scrolls, and rescue effects
summary: Consumable thresholds and unusual equipment behavior that raw stat lists do not explain.

sections.title: Potions and rations
paragraphs: Healing Potion triggers below 33% health and heals 70 × item quality × the wearer’s healing-done multiplier. Greater Healing Potion uses 180. The wearer’s healing-taken traits then apply. Each consumes the Potion slot. They have hooks in war, quest, arena, and dungeon healing.

Energy Potion triggers below 33% energy, restores 40 × quality, and consumes the Potion slot. Regeneration Potion instead heals 6 × quality on every supported hook and is not consumed by that helper. Rations multiply requested training by 1 + 0.25 × quality.

Lifebearer (Amulet of Healing) multiplies healing received by 1 + 0.2 × quality. Lifebloom heals 2 × quality to eligible rolled recipients: 100% chance for self in arena, 50% per quest party member, 80% per dungeon member. Its war chance uses integer 4 ÷ army count; armies above four therefore receive no Lifebloom healing from that hook.

sections.title: Group energy and resistance
paragraphs: Amulet of Energy restores 40 × quality to the party in quest/dungeon hooks when any member is below 30% energy, or when every member is at most 60%. It consumes the wearer’s Amulet. The energy helper’s ordered scan implements these thresholds.
Fire, Shadow, and Poison protection amulets grant their matching group resistance. Triune Shield grants all three only to its wearer. Resistance uses the highest-quality active source.
Fireball Amulet adds 45 × quality × wearer damage multiplier to war PartialProgress on war hooks and dungeon StageProgress on dungeon healing hooks. It does not use a separate attack entity.

sections.title: Scrolls
paragraphs: Healing Scroll triggers below 33% health, heals 220 × quality × wearer healing-done multiplier, and consumes Scroll. Group Healing Scroll heals 80 × quality × wearer healing-done multiplier: it triggers when anyone is below 35% health, or everyone is at most 65%. War recipients use integer 4 ÷ army count as their chance, so larger armies can consume it without healing recipients.

Damage Scroll adds 4 × wearer CombatPower on the fifth active combat tick of each boss stage. The hook does not consume it and does not directly multiply this extra hit by item quality or damage-trait multiplier.

Energy Scroll restores 30 × quality using the same 30% / 60% group-energy thresholds. Its helper removes Amulet rather than Scroll. In this installed implementation it can therefore remove an equipped amulet while retaining the scroll.

sections.title: Divine protection
paragraphs: Pontiff Ring applies DivineProtection as an aura; Martyr Relic supplies DivineProtection2 on its wearer. When pending damage is at least current health, the protection heals maximum health through normal healing and returns zero incoming damage. Martyr Relic removes Trinket.

The ring branch, in dungeon context, removes Pontiff Rings from party members but asks to remove DivineProtection2 buffs rather than DivineProtection. Stored/aura refresh behavior means it should not be described as a guaranteed clean one-charge effect. Its cleanup branch is also dungeon-specific. These are code-observed exceptions, not promises about intended design.

title: Nightmare adventure scaling and final rewards
summary: How repeated endgame victories change Ironcrag Siege and Tomb of Sholrath.

sections.title: Active scaling
paragraphs: When Nightmare is active, Tomb of Sholrath uses these multipliers based on total NightmareCount N: stage difficulty ×(1 + 0.01N), stage health additionally ×(1 + 0.05N), and supply cost ×(1 + 0.1N). Difficulty is rounded first, then health is calculated and cast to a long after the extra health multiplier.

Because stage health already multiplies BaseHealth by the scaled difficulty, effective health grows from both the difficulty and dedicated health factors. Dungeon challenge checks and damage also rise with the scaled difficulty.

Ironcrag Siege is the endgame war. While Nightmare is active, its maximum progress uses ×(1 + 0.05N); enemy strength and damage use ×(1 + 0.01N). Its stage-completion branch still compares progress to the stage’s declared ProgressAmount, so do not interpret the scaled MaxProgress property as an unconditional replacement of every completion threshold.

sections.title: Reward readiness
paragraphs: Fragmented Nightmare rewards are ready while Nightmare is active, or for the very first victory when NightmareCount is zero. Their base reward is two items.

Distilled Nightmare is ready for the first victory regardless of activity state, or afterward when Nightmare is active and NightmareProgress exceeds 0.99. When ready it increases NightmareCount by one and subtracts one progress only if progress is at least 1.

A Distilled Nightmare reward resets Ironcrag’s final hold: a completed front is moved back to zero-based stage 3, and that stage’s progress is set to 10. The Tomb’s current availability requirement is final Ironcrag completion, so another attempt depends on restoring that war condition.
The first ready Distilled reward also opens the game’s victory popup. Reaching the last boss is therefore distinct from qualifying for every repeat reward.
